most_likely_actual_diagnosis_free_text: Secondary syphilis, nodular or malignant (lues maligna) type, possibly with undiagnosed HIV co-infection
one_line_reason: The rash covers the palms and soles and comes with solitary nodules. Add diffuse lymphadenopathy, severe pharyngitis, headache, arthralgia and constitutional symptoms over 3 months with high CRP/ESR, and this is a classic secondary syphilis picture. The prolonged aPTT fits syphilis-associated antiphospholipid/lupus anticoagulant activity.
